question: Small marks of the editor chrome: where a dragged block panel can go, how the grid is drawn, and more as items need them.
how: real mouse input in headless Chrome on the demo page, plus DOM reads and screenshots. Nothing was saved: every run ended with Exit, and when the holds had changed the page, with Exit in the Exit Without Saving dialog.

panelMove.note: Shape block's Edit panel. A drag follows the pointer inside limits that depend on the window, not on the editor area. Escape closes it; it reopens at its first place.

grid.drawn: one absolute div per grid row (grid-area r / 1 / r / -1, as wide as the section), z-index auto, holding one absolute svg with a pattern and a rect filled by it
grid.svg: height 100%, left L, width calc(100% - (2L - 1)px), where L is the first track plus the column gap, rounded
grid.pattern: width (svg width + gap - 1) / columns, height 100%, patternUnits userSpaceOnUse
grid.cell: rect x 0.5, y 0.5, rx 3, stroke-width 1, stroke #B7B7B7, fill #F2F2F240, width tile - gap - 1, height row height - 1
grid.fade: in: opacity 0 to 0.65, transition opacity 0.1s ease-in, sampled at 0.33, 0.48, 0.65 over about 100 ms. Out: the first sample after the drop already reads 0, 46 ms later (one sample)
grid.startsAt: Below the 10px drag start the rows are in the page at opacity 0, on every section and with height 31 on the rect; nothing shows. The drag sets the height above and shows them

boxOnlyAlso.note: read before the drag starts, so with no cell height

grid.pixels: Same demo section, same scroll, 14px hold at 1600 by 1000: in the box x 100 to 860, y 400 to 700 of the window (empty cells only) ours and the oracle differ by 0 in every color channel. Phone: one row across the cells, x 586 to 1014, the same but for the 3 pixels of the oracle's center line (x 799 to 801), which ours does not draw on phones
grid.phoneRows: How many rows a phone hold shows is not settled: 14 after two desktop holds in the same session, 20 on the first hold of a fresh session. Ours shows 14. The look of a cell is the same in both
